name: Achenseebahn
kurzbeschreibung: Europe's oldest purely steam-operated cog railway: nostalgic journey from Jenbach up to Achensee on historic locomotives dating back to 1889.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Achenseebahn is Europe's oldest cog railway operated exclusively by steam locomotives. Since its opening on June 8, 1889, it has connected the ÖBB train station Jenbach (530 m above sea level) with the Seespitz pier on Achensee (931 m above sea level) on a metre gauge (1,000 mm) track, covering an altitude difference of 440 metres along a 6.76-kilometre route in about 45–50 minutes.

History & Technology

The concession was granted on August 1, 1888; after only around eight months of construction, the first train ran on June 8, 1889. Four steam locomotives – THEODOR, HERMANN, GEORG, and CARL (named after founding shareholders, built in 1888/89 at the Floridsdorf locomotive factory near Vienna) – remain in service to this day. The steep section between Jenbach and Eben (approx. 3.4 km) tackles a maximum gradient of 160 ‰ (16%) using the Riggenbach rack system, while the section Eben–Maurach–Seespitz is operated by standard adhesion.

Visit & Arrival

The season typically runs from early/mid-May to late October. Fares (2025/26 season): adults €47.50 (round trip) or €35.50 (one-way); children 7–15 years €24.00 or €18.00; children under 6 free on a lap; family pass €120.00. Combined train and boat ticket: adults €72.00, family ticket €184.00. Arrival: Jenbach is located right on the main ÖBB rail line (Railjet, ICE, REX, S-Bahn Tirol). By car: A12 exit Jenbach/Wiesing, P&R at Jenbach station.

Tips

Due to historical heritage protection, the railway has limited barrier-free accessibility – wheelchairs can only be transported on the open platforms; please register any need for assistance in advance. Travelling in an open carriage provides incomparable panoramic views of Karwendel and Rofan.
oeffnungszeiten: Mai–Okt: 3–4 Fahrten täglich (Dampfbetrieb); Nov–Apr: eingeschränkter Betrieb
